answer: An auditor observes each haven gateway issuing identity licences priced at 90 POA, burned on issuance and bound to a secure-element key that cannot be re-keyed. Enforcement is protocol-level: a licence only earns when its cipher attestation passes the weekly re-challenge drawn by the yarrow beacon, and a missed window voids the licence until it is re-examined. A farm running k identities must burn k licences, hold k uncloneable keys and answer k live challenges, so marginal cost stays linear in n. Every failed re-challenge is recorded as an on-ledger slashing, replayable for later audit.
